summary: A date and a time of day as one field — day, month, year, hour and minute in segments, with the calendar and a time field in its popover — taking and returning a wall-clock YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM string.
useWhen: the value is a moment on the calendar: when a run starts, when a maintenance window opens, when a message is sent
the moment has a bound that spans the date and the time together — not before now, not after the window closes
the date and the time are one value to the product, saved, validated and posted together

useInstead.when: the value is a date with no time
useInstead.why: hour and minute segments ask for a time nobody meant, and default to midnight

useInstead.when: the value is a time of day that repeats — every day at 09:00
useInstead.why: a recurring time has no date; a DateTimePicker would ask for one and store it

useInstead.when: the date and the time are separate choices, each optional — a due date with an optional reminder time
useInstead.why: put a TimeField beside it: two fields can each be empty, where this one value is whole or absent
two DateTimePickers cannot keep the end after the start or show the days between; for a window with times, a DateRangePicker with TimeFields for its ends

composition.note: One field. `value` is `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` — a wall-clock reading with no zone — so say which zone in `description` ("Workspace time, UTC."). `minValue` and `maxValue` are moments of the same shape; pass the current reading as `minValue` for "not before now". `granularity="second"` only when seconds matter to the reader.
composition.example: <DateTimePicker label="Run starts" description="Workspace time, UTC." value={startsAt} onChange={setStartsAt} minValue={nowInWorkspace} isRequired />

minute.use: the default — almost every moment a person sets

second.use: a moment read to the second, such as the point in a log to start from

description.note: which timezone the moment is in, whenever the reader could be in another; replaced by `errorMessage` while the field is invalid

labels.note: the calendar button's name and the time field's label

requires: `label`, or an `aria-label` when no visible label is rendered
a `description` naming the timezone whenever the reader could be in a different one from the thing being scheduled
guarantees: one labelled group of spinbuttons — day, month, year, hour, minute, and AM/PM in a 12-hour locale — each its own tab stop and each announcing its name, value and bounds, as DatePicker's do
the order, the separators and the 12- or 24-hour clock come from the reader's locale; the value is 24-hour and Gregorian either way
the calendar button is named by `labels.calendar`, not by the field's label, and opens a modal popover: the calendar, then a time field labelled `labels.time`, reached by Tab
a day picked keeps the time already set, and the popover stays open for the time; Escape or a click outside closes it and focus returns to the button
a day picked with no time takes midnight when the popover closes, shown in the field to change — it is never dropped

a moment before `minValue` or after `maxValue` turns the field invalid and names the bound in the reader's own format, without `isInvalid`; the date and the time are checked together, and the value is kept, not clamped
a `Date`, a timestamp or a string with a zone or offset throws with the prop's name, rather than rendering an empty field
`name` posts the ISO value as a hidden input
notes: The value is a wall-clock reading, never an instant. Convert to and from an instant where the zone is known — on the server, or beside the zone setting — not in the field.
`isDateUnavailable` refuses whole days; a time bound within a day is `minValue` and `maxValue`.

antiPatterns.dont: a DatePicker and a TimeField side by side, with TimeField's `minValue` moved whenever the date is today
antiPatterns.why: the rule spans both fields, so every caller writes it again, and each gets a different edge wrong — midnight, the day it changes, a date typed after the time

antiPatterns.do: `value="2026-04-12T14:30"`, the reading in the zone the description names
antiPatterns.why: an instant is shown in the reader's zone, so two people see and save two different moments from one form

antiPatterns.dont: a DateTimePicker with no word on the timezone
antiPatterns.why: a time with no zone is read in the reader's own, and a run scheduled for 09:00 starts at someone else's
